question: How do the existing spot-reclaim and spot-lead filters change when only the previously unparseable but otherwise valid Binance Spot H1 rows are retained?

design.one_variable: Use the newly repaired event panel, with unchanged frozen V1.7 candidates and unchanged event geometry. The parser excludes the original bad close_time rows without timestamp correction; events requiring those hours remain unknown.
design.placebo_strata: Same completed 12H entry_ms, direction, and frozen-score availability as the corresponding filter; use the existing wallet.sample_placebo implementation.
design.account: Reuse the existing wallet.compare_filter logic and existing hourly-capped VectorBT account (1000U, nine slots, NAV/10 sizing, 2/3 resting 2R and 1/3 runner, 20% hourly single-name cap; 5bp taker and 2bp maker). Existing old-panel account outputs are reused when the exact filter cohort membership is unchanged; only changed cohort comparisons are replayed.

checks.signal_stability: Every event already observed in the old panel must keep the same reclaim decision; every event with a previously observed lead value must keep the same signed log difference and lead sign.
checks.panel_identity: All 23,262 frozen event IDs appear exactly once in both old and repaired panels.
checks.account_reuse: Reuse old account outputs for an arm only when its exact old and new candidate membership sets are identical; otherwise use the existing VectorBT order callback once for that arm.
checks.fees: For replayed arms, record exact VectorBT order-record fees. Historical v1 funded files contain net cash PnL but no per-order fee total; do not infer the missing baseline fee ledger.
